title: agent-bureau: the console surface joins the train — release.json, the thin stub, and release-console.sh as the one rollout implementation deploy-console.sh also calls
body:
**Rewritten 2026-09-05 14:45 PT (re-plan).** The train's rules — lanes, collapse, spacing, window, green-at-SHA, the brake — live in bureau-pipeline's reusable workflow ([DRE-3167](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3167)). This card is the console SURFACE only: the data, the stub, the one release script, the operator caller's refusal, and the identity grant written as code. Earlier text on this card described a `rollout` job and a `CONSOLE_AUTO_ROLLOUT` repo variable inside `console-release.yml`; both are gone. The per-surface switch is `auto` in the data, and `console-release.yml` is NOT touched — it keeps building and pushing the two images on every console merge, and the release script consumes them the way `deploy-console.sh` does today.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `deploy-console.sh` and the train both run `infra/release-console.sh`; the rollout steps exist once (a test greps `deploy-console.sh` for `start-deployment` and finds none)
- [ ] `infra/test/rollback/test_release_console.py` runs the real script against the stub world and pins: a failed migration aborts before any `start-deployment` and cuts no tag; a failed rollout prints the rollback command and cuts no tag; a missing ECR image is a failure and never a build; a CDK change since the newest tag exits 0, cuts no tag and prints the `deferred:` line; a clean run rolls only the services whose digest changed, then cuts the tag
- [ ] `scripts/test_check_train_in_flight.py` pins exit 1 with the run URL on an in-flight run, exit 0 on none, exit 2 when `gh` fails; and `bash infra/deploy-console.sh` refuses, naming the run, under a fake `gh` that reports one
- [ ] `.github/bureau/release.json` on `main` holds the console entry exactly as stated above, `auto: false`, and no other surface
- [ ] `.github/workflows/release-train.yml` is the stub above and `make check-channel` passes (`@stable` and `pipeline_ref: stable`)
- [ ] The CDK synth test pins every new action to its resource ARN; nothing in this card runs `cdk deploy`, sets a variable, or flips `auto`
- [ ] `python3 .bureau-pipeline/scripts/check_tdd_commits.py origin/main HEAD` exits 0 before the push
**Blocked by:** DRE-3167

**Files:** .github/workflows/release-train.yml, .github/bureau/release.json, infra/release-console.sh, infra/deploy-console.sh, infra/test/rollback/test_release_console.py, scripts/check_train_in_flight.py, scripts/test_check_train_in_flight.py, infra/lib/release-stack.ts, infra/test/release-stack.test.ts, Makefile, infra/DEPLOY.md

title: bureau-pipeline: the reusable release train — one workflow_call every repo's stub consumes, the release.json schema and its check, the fleet-wide brake, and the collapse / spacing / window / green-at-SHA rules with a Python harness
body:
The engine half of [DRE-3164](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-3164/epic-the-release-train-one-reusable-train-in-bureau-pipeline-a-thin). The train is the ninth reusable workflow in this repo, in the shape of the other eight ([DRE-2553](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-2553/step-4-pin-agent-bureau-and-bureau-pipeline-to-the-channel-and-fold)): consumed by a thin stub per product repo that rides `@stable` and passes `pipeline_ref: stable`. It contains no product's deploy steps.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `tests/test_release_train.py` green on the six rules above; the harness is Python, never bash
- [ ] A stub consisting of data plus one `uses:` line runs the train against a fake surface script in the harness and produces one release, one tag, one receipt line
- [ ] The brake variable stops every surface, pinned
- [ ] Addendum rules pinned in the harness: a hand dispatch with `surface` runs an `auto: false` surface and still refuses on a red SHA and on `RELEASE_HOLD`; a pending check is waited for and refused after 30 minutes with the check named; a script that exits 0 printing `deferred: …` is reported as a no-op with no tag and no failure; a surface whose `paths` are untouched since its newest tag is a no-op that says so; the two scheduled firings decide by the `America/Los_Angeles` clock — a 06:00 PST firing is a no-op that names the window, an 08:00 PDT firing is an ordinary run
- [ ] This repo's own `.github/bureau/release.json` declares `pipeline-channel` with `record: channel`; the schema check accepts it and refuses a `channel` surface that names a script, and refuses `auto: true` with a null `script` or `rollback`
- [ ] `check_tdd_commits.py origin/main HEAD` exits 0 before the push

**Files:** dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/.github/workflows/release-train.yml, dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/scripts/release_train.py, dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/tests/test_release_train.py, dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/standards/release-train.md, dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/.github/bureau/release.json — every path is in bureau-pipeline, written with the repo prefix because the agent-bureau and portico cards in this epic share these file names in their own repos

title: agent-bureau: the relay joins the train — release-relay.sh as the one rollout implementation deploy.sh also calls, a rollback-relay command, the relay's release.json entry, and the Lambda grant written for the operator to apply
body:
The relay joins the train, second after the console. Today `cloud/relay/deploy.sh` does everything by hand: provisions the Secrets Manager entries from the operator's `.env`, ensures the role and the function URL, builds the wheel zip, `update-function-code`, stamps `DEPLOYED_SHA`/`DEPLOYED_AT` into the Lambda environment, reads the sha back off the live function, and cuts `agent-bureau-relay-v<N>` from the read-back (DRE-2789). This card splits that into the half only an operator may run and the half a release is:

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `deploy.sh` and the train both run `infra/release-relay.sh`; the code-update, stamp, read-back and tag steps exist once (a test greps `deploy.sh` for `update-function-code` and finds none)
- [ ] The Python harness pins: the environment write-back keeps every pre-existing key and changes exactly `DEPLOYED_SHA`/`DEPLOYED_AT`; a failed `update-function-code` exits non-zero and cuts no tag; `ROLLBACK=1` cuts no forward tag
- [ ] `make rollback-relay VERSION=<tag>` exists, refuses an unknown tag, and prints the sha it will stamp before touching AWS (`DRY=1`)
- [ ] `bash cloud/relay/deploy.sh` refuses, naming the run, when a fake `gh run list` reports a release-train run in flight
- [ ] `release.json` on `main` has the relay entry with `auto: false`; the CDK test asserts the four Lambda actions are scoped to the relay function ARN and nothing broader
- [ ] Nothing in this card runs `cdk deploy`, sets a variable or flips `auto`
- [ ] `python3 .bureau-pipeline/scripts/check_tdd_commits.py origin/main HEAD` exits 0 before the push

**Files:** infra/release-relay.sh, cloud/relay/deploy.sh, infra/rollback-relay.sh, Makefile, .github/bureau/release.json, infra/lib/release-stack.ts, infra/test/release-stack.test.ts, scripts/test_relay_deploy_record.py, infra/DEPLOY.md, infra/test/rollback/test_release_relay.py

title: agent-bureau: the website joins the train — release-website.sh as the one implementation deploy-website.sh also calls, invalidation waited on and verified, the website's release.json entry, and the S3/CloudFront grant written for the operator to apply
body:
The website joins the train in the relay's shape. Today `infra/deploy-website.sh` builds `website/` with the node its `.nvmrc` declares, syncs `website/dist` to the private S3 bucket the `MarketingSiteStack` (us-east-1) owns, invalidates the CloudFront distribution, and cuts `agent-bureau-website-v<M>.<m>.<b>` (the legacy `website-v*` series is read so the counter continues). The last website release was `website-v1.0.2` on 2026-06-16; nothing has been cut since because a hand has to run it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `deploy-website.sh` and the train both run `infra/release-website.sh`; the sync, invalidate and tag steps exist once
- [ ] The Python harness pins: a failed sync or a failed verify exits non-zero and cuts no tag; the invalidation is waited on before the verify; the tag's annotation carries sha, timestamp, bucket and distribution as today
- [ ] `make deploy-website` refuses, naming the run, when a fake `gh run list` reports a release-train run in flight
- [ ] `release.json` on `main` has the website entry with `auto: false`; the CDK test asserts the S3 and CloudFront actions are scoped to the context-named bucket and distribution
- [ ] Nothing in this card runs `cdk deploy` or flips `auto`

title: PROOF: the release train observed live on the console — the unattended rollout and its receipt, the collapse, spacing, window, brake, operator-refusal and failure-alert rules, recorded in the repo
body:
**Scope after the 2026-09-06 split: the CONSOLE surface only.** This proof records the rules observed on the console's first supervised release and its first unattended one (DRE-3166): the unattended rollout and its receipt, the collapse, the spacing, the window, the green-checks rule, the stop switch, the hand-deploy refusal and the failure alert. The fleet-wide proof — one unattended rollout per joined surface, and deploy-lag reading its surface table from `release.json` — belongs to part 2, epic DRE-3245 (the eight cards moved there: DRE-3212, DRE-3213, DRE-3214, DRE-3215, DRE-3216, DRE-3217, DRE-3218, DRE-3238), and is written when that epic is planned. Re-scoped 2026-09-06 after the second critic found this card still waiting on those eight cards.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The record exists on `main` with one section per rule (unattended rollout, collapse, spacing, window, brake, operator refusal, failure alert), each citing the live observation made by hand on the console, with a PT timestamp and the run URL or tag it left behind
- [ ] The unattended-rollout section links the merged PR, the train run, the `agent-bureau-console-v*` tag it cut and the Shipped-today panel reading Pending release 0 afterwards
- [ ] The brake section records `RELEASE_HOLD` set, the merge that did not roll out while it was set, and the rollout that followed once it was cleared
- [ ] The operator-refusal section records `make deploy-console` refusing during an in-flight train run, with the run URL it named
- [ ] The failure section records the CRITICAL `release_train:agent-bureau` alert as it appeared on the Alerts feed and the absence of a tag for that run
- [ ] The record closes with a deploy-lag reading taken after the unattended release, in the same minute as the panel, showing the console current
- [ ] The record names what it does NOT prove — the relay, the website, portico's portals, and deploy-lag reading its surfaces from `release.json` — and points at DRE-3245, where that proof is written
**Deferred to part 2 (DRE-3245):** one section per further surface — relay, website, portico's portals — naming its first unattended release, and the section showing the console's `deployLag` and `make deploy-lag` reading the same `release.json` data. None of that work is in this epic any more, so none of it can be observed here.
